Team / Susan — I reviewed the attached PDF and drafted the internal acceptance checklist we use in tax ops. Susan — I'm pasting the checklist here so your AP team can validate before we do any manual work: 

TAX EXEMPTION ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST (Redwood Tax Ops)
- Certificate type: state-form OR multi-jurisdiction blanket (we accept both; state form preferred).
- Seller name exact match: certificate must show "Redwood Inference" or "Redwood Inference, Inc." — mismatches require a signed affidavit.
- Effective date / expiration: certificate must be valid on date of invoice.
- Signatory authority: signer name + title must appear (we confirm title with LinkedIn/company page if unclear).
- Covered locations: document must either list ship-to address(es) or be a blanket certificate that explicitly covers our ship-to locations.
- Readable PDF and signed image: we need a legible signature block; DocuSign summary/receipt is acceptable proof.
- Supporting doc (optional but speeds review): purchase order showing business use or a reseller account registration.

If all criteria are satisfied we will: 
- Clear the invoice hold for Invoice #7893.
- Apply exemption prospectively to shipments after the effective date and, upon request, retroactively to invoices back to the date you specify (subject to state rules).

Next steps for Aurora to get the fastest result:
1) Confirm whether the attached PDF is a state form or a company blanket certificate.
2) If you want retroactive relief to 2026-07-01, confirm in this thread.
3) Upload DocuSign receipt or a brief signed authority email from Lisa Tran (VP Finance).

I’ve attached a one-page "tax-acceptance-checklist.pdf" (stub) you can reuse. Once we have the confirmation we’ll clear the hold and post confirmation to the HubSpot deal record.

Ben Carter
Senior Tax Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
